sentences.text: It is submitted that present is a case of false impli alternative it is submitted that, at best, it may be a case of non-penetrative sexual assault and by no stretch of imagination, provisions of Section 5(m) of POCSO Act will be attracted as there is no penetrative sexual assault on a child below 12 years.

6 . Thus, it is submitted that as per the report of lady doctor, Smt. Ankita Patel (PW-7), it being a case of non-penetrative sexual assault which is corroborated from the evidence of the DNA examination as has been brought on record by the State vide I.A. No.1646/2025, at best, it will be a case under Section 7 of POCSO Act, punishable under Section 8 of POCSO Act.
7.
It is, thus, submitted that it being a case of false accusation, appellant may be acquitted or in the alternate his conviction may be modified.

8. Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor for the State, in his turn, submits that as far as provisions of the SC/ST Act are concerned, they NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50416 3 CRA-5266-2025 will be attracted and, therefore, no leniency can be shown in the matter.

9 . After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record.
10. PW-1 is the School Teacher, he has proved date of birth of the victim to be 12.09.2017, therefore,
at the time of the incident victim was about 6 years of age.
11. PW-2 is the mother of the victim, who has partly supported the case of the prosecution and for another part, she was declared hostile and leading questions were put to her.

In cross-examination,
she has admitted that accused Rahman @ Chand used to visit their house along with his wife for work, therefore, he known to her.
Several suggestions have been given but her evidence has largely remained unrebutted.
1 2 . Victim (PW-3) has admitted in cross-examination that appellant Rahman is known to her.
He had worked at her house, therefore, he used to visit their house again and again to claim his amounts.
Thereafter, she stated that he was drunk.
She admitted that on account of money transactions there was a dispute between her parents and Rahman.
She admitted that there are discrepancies in the statements of her parents.
She stated that saliva was put on her forehead as well as on private parts.

However, she has not stated anything about penetrative sexual assault or in Mohammad Rahman Qureshi @ Chand vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21304354/
2 regard to aggravated penetrative sexual assault as defined in Section 5 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 13. As far as lady Doctor, Smt. Ankita Patel (PW-7) has categorically stated that she had not noticed any injury on the private parts of the victim, her hymen was intact.
Thus, in view of the evidence of the lady doctor, Smt. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50416 4 CRA-5266-2025 Ankita Patel, it is evident that present is not a case of penetrative sexual assault.
14. As far as DNA report dated 29.09.2025 is concerned, it makes a clear mention that victim's vaginal slide, vaginal swab and swab per vagina did not reveal any Y-Chromosome STR DNA profile.
It is also mentioned that human saliva was found on her Pajama, Ex. D, and that was put to test.
In the test, DNA profile obtained from the blood sample of the accused was found to be present on the Pajama, Article D, of the victim.

Thus, when the oral testimony of the victim and that of medical evidence is taken into consideration, then present being a case of non-penetrative sexual assault as defined in Section 7, therefore, conviction of the appellant cannot be maintained under Section 5(m)/6 of POCSO Act and it needs to be altered and is hereby altered to Section 7/8 of POCSO Act.
15. As far as appellant's conviction under Section 363, 366 and 342 of IPC is concerned, that deserves to be maintained and is hereby maintained.
However, his conviction under Section 376-AB being not made out, is hereby set aside.

Similarly, appellant's conviction under Section 5(m)/6 being also not made out, is hereby set aside and it is substituted with conviction under Section 7/8 of POCSO Act with 5 years of Rigorous Imprisonment and Fine of Rs.1000/- (Rupees One Thousand Only) with default stipulation of 1 years.

16. As far as conviction under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act is concerned, this provision as contained in the SC/ST Act provides that if a person commits any offence under the Indian Penal Code punishable with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50416 5 CRA-5266-2025 imprisonment for a term of 10 years or more against a person of property (knowing that such person is a member of a scheduled caste or a scheduled tribe or such property belongs to such member)
shall be punishable with imprisonment for life and with fine.
17.

Though Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor submits that conviction under Section 3(2)(v) is required to be maintained but looking to the fact that this Court has set aside the conviction under Section 376-AB so also under Section 5(m)/6, then when the provisions of Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act are examined, then offence under Section 7 of the POCSO Act being punishable with minimum 3 years of sentence and maximum 5 years of sentence, we have no hesitation to hold that provisions of Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act will not be attracted and, therefore, impugned conviction under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST cannot be sustained.
However, conviction of the appellant under Section 3(1)(w)(i) is maintained.
It is directed that all the sentences shall run concurrently.
18. In above terms, this Criminal Appeal is partly allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction is modified.
The case property be disposed off in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
Record of the trial Court be sent back.
19. Record of the trial Court be sent immediately.
